guarantees.claim: u_prim_flop_ab_gamma10_q updates {a_gamma1_qq,a_gamma0_qq,b_gamma1_qq,b_gamma0_qq} from {a_gamma1_q,a_gamma0_q,b_gamma1_q,b_gamma0_q} on rising clk_i when we_i[1] is high and rst_ni is de-asserted high; asserts zero on all outputs when rst_ni is low.
guarantees.cond: always, synchronous to clk_i and rst_ni

guarantees.claim: u_prim_flop_ab_omega_buf updates {a_omega_buf_q,b_omega_buf_q} from {a_omega_buf,b_omega_buf} on rising clk_i when we_i[1] is high and rst_ni is de-asserted high; asserts zero on all outputs when rst_ni is low.
guarantees.cond: always, synchronous to clk_i and rst_ni

assumptions.claim: The input signals a_gamma1_q, a_gamma0_q, b_gamma1_q, b_gamma0_q, a_omega_buf, b_omega_buf must be stable and valid at the rising edge when we_i[1] is asserted.
assumptions.risk: If any input is stale or invalid, the captured mask share values may be corrupted, potentially breaking DOM security and exposing secret data.

assumptions.claim: rst_ni must be asserted low for a sufficient number of clock cycles to reset both flop instances before any operational use.
assumptions.cond: at initial power-up or during global reset
assumptions.risk: If reset is not properly applied, the flop outputs may hold unknown or stale values, leading to use of uninitialized mask shares, which can break masking security and leak secrets.

uncertain_points.claim: The enable signal we_i[1] is used to update both mask share registers simultaneously. Without cross-chunk verification, it is unclear whether we_i[1] is properly sequenced to prevent capture of invalid or zero mask shares during active computation.
uncertain_points.cond: when we_i[1] transitions to 1 during an active cipher round
uncertain_points.risk: If we_i[1] is asserted before valid mask shares are generated or after a reset, the flops may load all‑zero or stale values, breaking DOM security and potentially leaking intermediate key‑dependent values.

uncertain_points.claim: Both flop instances reset to all zeros (ResetValue = '0). If the module begins a computation cycle without first loading fresh random mask values into these registers, all mask shares will be zero, effectively disabling DOM masking and exposing secret data.
uncertain_points.cond: after reset deassertion and before any valid mask load
uncertain_points.risk: Zero mask shares during a multiplication in the AES S‑box can cause unmasked intermediate results to appear on side‑channels, compromising key extraction.
